title: Recent Flash Floods and Adequacy of Drainage System
what_it_is: Recent Flash Floods and Adequacy of Drainage System

sections.label: Parliamentary questions on January 2018 flooding
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources about the 8 January 2018 flash flood at Bedok North Avenue 4 and flooding at nine eastern locations.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources with regard to the flash flood on 8 January 2018 at Bedok North Avenue 4 (a) whether the ongoing enhancement drainage works at Bedok Canal was one of the reasons that limits the water capacity that can be stored or discharged through the canal during heavy downpours and high tides; (b) if so, what are the interim measures to prevent potential flash floods at this area until enhancement works are completed in 2019; and (c) what measures are in place to ensure the public living and working near any canals are alerted before possible water overflow occurs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) what current mechanisms are in place to notify motorists of impending flash floods in order to redirect traffic from affected areas; and (b) whether such mechanisms can be further enhanced to achieve broader and more effective notifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (a) what caused the heavy flooding at the nine locations in the eastern part of Singapore on 8 January 2018; (b) whether each location has a history of flooding; (c) whether existing drainage works is a cause; (d) what measures have been taken to assist members of the public who were affected by the flooding; and (e) what measures will be taken to prevent similar flooding.

sections.label: Highest recorded rainfall
sections.summary: The highest recorded total rainfall on that morning was 118.8 millimetres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The highest recorded total rainfall on that morning was 118.8 millimetres.

sections.label: Drainage investment and Bedok Canal widening
sections.summary: The Government invested $1.2 billion and set aside $500 million, while Bedok Canal is widened from 38 to 44 metres at $128 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The Government has invested $1.2 billion on these works and has set aside another $500 million for the next two to three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Bedok Canal, which serves some of the affected areas, is being widened at a cost of $128 million to expand its width from 38 metres to 44 metres, wide enough to accommodate an expressway of 10 lanes, five lanes each way.

sections.label: Flood receptor features for buildings
sections.summary: PUB stipulates that buildings in areas most at risk of flooding must have receptor features to prevent floodwaters from damaging them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For areas that are most at risk of flooding, PUB stipulates that buildings must have receptor features, such as higher platform levels, crest protection and flood barriers to prevent floodwaters from damaging them.

sections.label: Convective thunderstorms and flood management
sections.summary: Convective thunderstorms limit warning lead time, and the comprehensive flood management approach seeks to alleviate risks while minimising disruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: These weather systems comprise mainly convective thunderstorms which tend to be localised, develop rather suddenly, and are of short duration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This limits the lead time of our warnings of heavy rain and consequently of the flash floods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Our approach to flood management is a comprehensive one that seeks to alleviate flood risks while minimising disruption to the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We will continue to take all necessary steps to enhance flood resilience in Singapore and keep the public informed of flash flood incidents.

sections.label: Priorities and extent of drainage network
sections.summary: It states the need to look at conditions, speed and priorities, and notes Singapore has 8,000 kilometres of drains, canals and rivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Therefore, when we look at our problems, we have to look at conditions of what we need to do and how fast we can do what, and which we should put priorities on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We have 8,000 kilometres (km) of drains, canals and rivers.

sections.label: Retention tank plan submissions
sections.summary: There are about 500 submissions for plans to do retention tanks for developments above 0.2 hectares.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For example, right now, there are about 500 submissions for plans to do retention tanks for those developments above 0.2 hectares.

sections.label: Action against contractors
sections.summary: In cases like Tampines Avenue 12, action is taken against the contractor, bringing them to Court and fining them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: When this happens, as in the recent case of Tampines Avenue 12, we will take action against the contractor, bring them to Court and fine them.
